newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: MCLACHLAN SAYS TANDEM THRUST A SUCCESS
The Defence Minister, Ian McLachlan, has visited Shoalwater Bay in central Queensland, to take a first hand look at Excercise Tandem Thrust.
Mr McLachlan says the excercise has been very successful, and there are likely to be more exercises with the US .
He says while there are no plans to establish a US military base in Australia, there has been some preliminary discussion on permanently locating some U-S equipment here.
ARENA SAYS MANY MORE ALLEGATIONS TO BE INVESTIGATED
New South Wales Labor MP Franca Arena says there's a brotherhood of paedophilia in the state which has not been fully exposed.
Mrs Arena says she's disappointed the Police Royal Commission has closed its public hearings, saying there are still many allegations of pedophilia which need to be investigated.

Mrs Arena says she'll be providing Police with information this week alleging two senior politicians, two legal figures, including a judge and a businessman, are involved in pedophilia. But Police Minister, Paul Whelan, says the Police Royal Commission has not closed, and will be able to investigate child sexual abuse claims until it brings down its pedophilia report in July.
MEDICAL AUTHORITIES FIND AIRPORT MALARIA CASE CHALLENGING
Medical authorities in far north Queensland say they found the case of a Cairns man, who contracted Malaria from a mosquito which came in on an overseas aircraft, very challenging.
Dr Scott Ritchie, from the Tropical Public Health Unit, says the chances of a repeat case are slim.
But he says Queensland's far north could be vulnerable to more cases of airport malaria, because of its close ties with Papua New Guinea.
KENNETT NOT ALARMED BY CLAIM
The Victorian Premier says Aboriginal groups are often after recognition of their soecial interests, and not always land or money, when they make native title claims.
Jeff Kennett says he's not alarmed by a mabo-style claim for almost 500 hectares of Wilson's Promontory, lodged at the Native Title Tribunal last Friday.
Aboriginal leaders say the Prom contains some significant historical sites, and a detailed archelogical study will be carried out.
Mr Kennett says the claim will probably be delayed for a decade because of uncertainty surrounding the Native Title Act.
APPLEBY WINS HONDA CLASSIC
Australian golfer Stewart Appleby has won the Honda Classic by one stroke from Payne Stewart in Florida.
Appleby finished on 14-under the card.
Appleby led after three rounds before losing the lead then regained it towards the end of the final round.
FIRST INDIGENOUS UNIVERSITY COLLEGE
A university college which caters entirely for indigenous students, will aim to provide a supportive community in which indigenous students can study.
The Mattanya College, which has opened in Adelaide and will take students from all over Australia, is attached to a mainstream uni.
Academic director, Haroon Hassan says it's the first of its type in a major Australian university.
